title: Generate Parentheses
interviewTips: Ask if order matters and if n=0 should return [''] or [] - LeetCode constraints say 1 <= n <= 8 and order does not matter.
Trade-off: brute force enumerates 2^(2n) strings vs backtracking prunes invalid prefixes to Catalan(n) ~ 4^n / n^(3/2) nodes vs DP builds answers bottom-up without invalid search.
Edge-case tip: enforce invariants open <= n and close <= open; never place ')' when close == open, and use mutable buffer with backtrack to keep O(n) auxiliary space.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Enumeration + Validation
approaches.intuition: Generate every string of length 2*n made of '(' and ')' then keep only balanced ones. This separates generation from correctness checking and is the simplest first-principles baseline.
approaches.theory: There are 2^(2n) binary strings. Build them via DFS choosing '(' or ')' at each position. When length reaches 2*n, validate with a balance counter: +1 for '(' and -1 for ')', invalid if balance ever negative or final balance != 0. Only valid strings are added to result.

timeComplexity.explanation: 2^(2n) = 4^n leaves, each validation scans O(n), so O(n * 4^n) time. Internal nodes double this but same order.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion depth 2*n and current string O(n), excluding output which holds Catalan(n) strings of length 2*n.

steps: Validate each: ((())) invalid length, (()) balance never negative and ends 0 -> keep

edgeCases: n=1 returns single element list with ()
n=8 max constraint still feasible but output size Catalan(8)=1430
Unbalanced prefixes like )... are generated then discarded, showing wastefulness

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal Backtracking with Open-Close Pruning
approaches.intuition: Only build prefixes that can still become valid: we can add '(' if we have used fewer than n, and we can add ')' only if it will not exceed number of '(' so far. This prunes all invalid branches early.
approaches.theory: Maintain counts open and close. Invariant: 0 <= close <= open <= n. At each step branch to '(' if open < n and to ')' if close < open. When length == 2*n we have a valid sequence. Search tree size equals Catalan number, which is optimal since we must output that many strings.

timeComplexity.explanation: Proportional to Catalan(n) = (1/(n+1)) * C(2n,n) ~ 4^n / (n^(3/2) * sqrt(pi)). Each valid string costs O(n) to build, often written as O(n * Catalan(n)).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion depth 2*n plus mutable buffer O(n), excluding output storage O(n * Catalan(n)).

steps: branch '(' -> '((' and '()' ; '()' branch continues to '()(' etc.
prune: never allow close > open, e.g., '())' not explored from '()' ? actually allowed, but ')(' at start never explored

edgeCases: n=1: open<1 allows '(' then close<open allows ')' => [()]

approaches.name: Approach 3: DP by Catalan Closure
approaches.intuition: Any valid sequence can be written as '(' + A + ')' + B where A is valid of size i and B is valid of size n-1-i. Build all answers for smaller n and combine.
approaches.theory: Let dp[k] be all well-formed strings with k pairs. dp[0] = ['']. For k>=1, for each split i in 0..k-1, for each left in dp[i], right in dp[k-1-i], form '(' + left + ')' + right. This enumerates Catalan decomposition without search and guarantees uniqueness. Memoization or iterative DP both work.

timeComplexity.explanation: Total combinations across all splits equals Catalan(n). String concatenation costs O(n) each, so O(n * Catalan(n)) ~ O(4^n / sqrt(n)).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Must store all intermediate dp tables; dp[n] alone holds Catalan(n) strings of length 2*n. Auxiliary excluding output is O(n) for loops.

edgeCases: n=0 (if allowed) returns list with empty string per base case
Duplicate avoidance: decomposition is unique so no dedup needed
n=8 creates 1430 strings, DP reuses subresults efficiently
